observation: Use case: precise-object-edit. Use the provided computer rendering as a strict geometric MATCH PLATE. Transform it into a genuinely photographic frame of the SAME physical spacecraft set, preserving exact room layout, camera position, eye level, lens, all outer silhouettes, locations of each fastening and aperture, object colors, and exact image crop. Do not move anything. Photograph it as a real advanced working pressure vessel at cinema quality, on a large-format documentary camera. Replace the schematic smooth CG surfaces with extremely believable material response: fine molded pearl aramid fairings with almost imperceptible manufacturing grain and contact grime, local edge polish, machined alloy and brush direction, diamond-polished instrument glass, subtle machining marks, fabrics woven at a visible scale with true seam relief. Beautiful but physically motivated soft bounced daylight from glazing and neutral recessed practicals, off-axis grazing shadows and contact shading, with detail readable in the practical shadow. Gray-balance with a slight cool Earth cast and muted orange-red harness accents. It MUST look like an actual photograph, not a game screenshot. Preserve exact alignment and proportions and only improve lighting, microdetails, human touch and optical fidelity. NOT steampunk, rusted, neon, futuristic hotel or a concept-art illustration. NO extra hardware that changes silhouettes, NO image labels or overlay. Landscape 16:9 full-bleed. Make the slate acceleration seat shells and red webbing especially convincing, with woven strap texture, embroidered safety flag, tension wrinkles and crisp machined belt hardware, the instrument panel flush glass with thin crisp flight data traces and backlit print. Keep the pressure window and its frame and mullion outlines unchanged. Outside keep a clean Earth horizon and no accessory props.
